title: Procedural Sneaker Customization (Shoe Customizer)
prompt:
Use Three.js to procedurally generate a simplified sneaker consisting of four parts: the sole, upper, tongue, and laces. Support changing the color and material type by region.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following import map in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Model]
(1) All four regions must be procedural meshes composed using BoxGeometry / Extrude / Lathe, etc., with a single shoe as the parent Group.
(2) id="zoneSelect": A <select> with four option names exactly matching zones[].name: "sole", "upper", "tongue", and "laces".
(3) id="zoneColor": An <input type="color" /> that changes the material color of the child mesh corresponding to the current selectedZone.
(4) id="zoneMaterial": A <select> with at least three types: "standard", "matte", and "glossy" (distinguished using roughness/metalness), applied to the current region.
(5) id="autoRotate": A checkbox that controls OrbitControls.autoRotate.

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  zones: [{ name: string, color: string, material: string }],  // The length must always be 4, in the same order as the four regions
  selectedZone: string,   // "sole"|"upper"|"tongue"|"laces"
  autoRotate: boolean
}

Output a single HTML file that runs when opened directly in a browser.
